kurz: Lactic acid bacteria turn warm milk into yoghurt overnight. A few spoonfuls of shop-bought yoghurt are enough as a starter.
bild_im_kopf: Like yeast in dough, only for milk: a few workers are enough, and overnight they become billions.
sicherheit: Work cleanly. If the yoghurt smells rotten, is pink or mouldy: throw it away.
ergebnis: About 1 l of yoghurt. Drained in a cloth, it becomes Greek yoghurt or labneh.
haltbarkeit: About a week in the fridge. Two spoonfuls of it are the starter for the next batch.
material: 2 tbsp natural yoghurt with live cultures
oven with the light on, or a hot-water bottle in a cool box
verwendung: For breakfast, for raita against spicy heat, for marinades.
Drained as labneh with olive oil.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Heat the milk to 85–90 °C and hold it for about 10 minutes
schluesselmomente.warum: The heat changes the [[molke|whey]] protein. Later it binds more water, and the [[joghurt|yoghurt]] turns thicker.
Yoghurt bacteria work best in this range. Above about 48 °C they die.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Stir a little milk smooth with the yoghurt, then mix everything
schluesselmomente.warum: That way the bacteria spread evenly.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Fill into jars and keep warm for 4–12 hours without moving them
schluesselmomente.warum: The bacteria turn [[milch|milk]] sugar into lactic acid. The acid makes the milk protein set into a gel.

schluesselmomente.schritt: As soon as it is firm, into the fridge
schluesselmomente.warum: Cold slows the bacteria: the longer it stays warm, the more sour it gets.
